senses.sense_definition: A person who ignores moral or sexual restraints and seeks pleasure without regard for social norms.

examples.text: The novel depicts a wealthy <w>libertine</w> who spends his nights chasing fleeting pleasures in the city.
He was known as a notorious <w>libertine</w> who cared little for the consequences of his reckless lifestyle.

senses.sense_definition: A person who holds unconventional or freethinking views regarding religion or established dogma.

examples.text: During the Enlightenment, many a <w>libertine</w> challenged the rigid religious doctrines of the time.
The philosopher was labeled a <w>libertine</w> for his radical rejection of traditional church authority.

senses.sense_definition: A person who was formerly a slave but has been granted their freedom, specifically in Ancient Rome.

examples.text: In Roman society, a <w>libertine</w> could eventually gain certain rights, though they remained socially distinct from citizens.
The status of a <w>libertine</w> was carefully recorded in the official census of the Roman Republic.

traits.comment: Refers to a specific historical social status in Ancient Rome.

senses.sense_definition: Lacking moral restraint or behaving in a way that ignores social and sexual standards.

examples.text: His <w>libertine</w> lifestyle eventually led to his complete social isolation from the community.
The play explores the consequences of a <w>libertine</w> attitude toward traditional marriage vows.
